claims.text: Ab initio Density Functional Theory calculations can determine whether a material has a ferromagnetic ground state.
The material under consideration is ferromagnetic at low temperature.
Exchange interaction and spin polarization lead to alignment of magnetic moments.
Exchange interaction favors parallel spin alignment.
Spin polarization enhances the magnetic moment.
Alignment of magnetic moments produces a ferromagnetic ground state.
The proposed mechanism produces a magnetic moment of at least 1.5 μB per atom.
The predicted state is a ferromagnetic ground state.
The predicted magnetic moment is at least 1.5 μB per atom.
The baseline magnetic moment is 1.25 μB per atom.
The baseline is a non-magnetic ground state.
A moment of at least 1.5 μB per atom is higher than the stated baseline of 1.25 μB per atom.
The exact temperature dependence of the magnetic moment is uncertain.
A calculated magnetic moment below 1.5 μB per atom would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial material is already labeled ferromagnetic, while the baseline is labeled a non-magnetic ground state and the prediction is the presence of a ferromagnetic ground state. The hypothesis does not explain whether the baseline refers to the same material or how DFT changes an initially ferromagnetic system into the predicted state.

The baseline is called non-magnetic while also being assigned a sizable magnetic moment of 1.25 μB per atom; no distinction between local and net magnetic moment is provided to reconcile these statements.
